Dense gas (negative buoyancy) criteria based on Release Richardson Number The gas density, ρ ,in the Richardson number equation, is determined from either g • the molecular weight of the gas or liquid, or • from field experiments involving liquid aerosols that behave like dense gases. The first method, based on a molecular weight comparison of the source material and the ambient atmosphere, is common for identifying dense gas materials. But with molecular weight being a static property, this determination alone would eliminate numerous chemicals from being classified as denser than air materials. The field experiment method goes beyond the first criteria by accounting for chemicals stored under pressure or lower temperatures, conditions which increase the physical density of the material. A well-known example is hydrogen fluoride (HF). Despite having a relatively low molecular weight, HF is commonly stored at conditions which can raise its density to values well beyond that of the surrounding air.
